## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

3	// `baselining`, and since Phase 5 deleted that, the only thing that maintains a

5	// held one is gone (#1252).

8	// (worker.mjs): they converge the mount, run the version-ranged migrations, gate on
9	// the converged tree's self-test, open the PR, and act on the terminal. The AGENT

11	// meeting member-authored content the canon has never seen.

13	// Self-contained (imports nothing) so the scheduler, executor, and a human all load
14	// it standalone — the whole contract lives in this default export.
15	
16	export default {
17	  id: 'update',
18	  frequency: 'daily',                    // the head of the morning chain — everything that reads a converged mount declares `schedule_after:` this
19	  precondition_signals: ['stamp', 'sharedMount'],

1	// Agent invocation (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §12, §14.6). The executor starts the
2	// agent session with an API CALL rather than by arming a label event, which is
3	// what retires the re-arm, the grace window and the transport dance — and what
4	// makes a lost hand-off a synchronous, visible failure at the executor instead of
5	// a label event fired into the void.
6	//
7	// A TASK NAMES AN ENDPOINT, NEVER A URL. The declaration is vendored verbatim
8	// into every consuming repo, so it must never carry deployment detail or anything
9	// adjacent to a credential: `invocation_endpoint: 'fleet'` names a key, and the
10	// repo's own config maps that key to a URL and to the NAME of the repo Actions
11	// secret holding its token. That indirection is also what replaces the whole
12	// self/fleet apparatus — reach is a property of which endpoint you call, so a
13	// task needing wider access names a different endpoint and nothing else in the
14	// system needs a concept of scope.
15	//
16	// THE PROMPT NAMES ONE ITEM AND CARRIES NO INSTRUCTIONS. Everything
17	// behavior-defining is read by the session from the tracked task files at HEAD;
18	// the prompt says which issue and which nonce, and the session validates both in
19	// code before acting (DESIGN §7).
20	
21	import { ENDPOINTS_KEY, LEGACY_ENDPOINTS_KEY } from '../../checks/helpers/repo-context.mjs';
22	
23	export const DEFAULT_ENDPOINT = 'default';
24	
25	// The endpoint is a ROUTINE'S API TRIGGER — `POST /v1/claude_code/routines/
26	// <trigger-id>/fire` with a per-routine bearer token — which is what Claude Code
27	// on the web actually exposes to an HTTP caller. Three consequences the design's
28	// "a CCR API call" did not spell out, each verified against the routines docs
29	// rather than assumed:
30	//
31	//  - THE BEHAVIOR IS THE ROUTINE'S STORED PROMPT, not ours. `text` reaches the
32	//    session wrapped in a `<routine-fire-payload>` block explicitly labelled
33	//    untrusted, and a routine acts on it only because its own saved prompt says
34	//    to. That is the issue-is-data posture arriving for free at one more hop: our
35	//    payload names an item, and every instruction comes from a stored artifact.
36	//    The routine's stored prompt is one line pointing at `instructions.md` beside
37	//    this file, so the whole of what a session does is tracked and reviewed.
38	//  - THE BODY CARRIES ONE FIELD. `text` is freeform and unparsed — structured
39	//    JSON would arrive as a literal string — so the item number and nonce go in
40	//    as prose, and nothing else goes in at all.
41	//  - THERE IS NO IDEMPOTENCY KEY (standing entry 11, answered: the endpoint
42	//    offers none), which is exactly why THIS MODULE CALLS ONCE PER ITEM AND NEVER
43	//    RETRIES. A retry is only safe when you know the first call did nothing, and
44	//    a client-side timeout is the one case where you cannot know — the session
45	//    may well have started. Retrying there is what would make invocation
46	//    at-least-once and put two sessions on one item; declining to retry is what
47	//    keeps it at-most-once and lets the whole agent-side claim protocol delete.
48	//    An outcome we did not learn is reported as UNKNOWN and resolved by the agent
49	//    leash, which is a rule that already exists, rather than by a guess here.
50	//
51	// The beta header is dated and the endpoint is a research preview whose two most
52	// recent header versions keep working, so it lives in config with a default here
53	// — a rotation is then a config edit on one repo, never an engine release the
54	// whole fleet waits for.
55	export const DEFAULT_HEADERS = Object.freeze({
56	  'anthropic-beta': 'experimental-cc-routine-2026-04-01',
57	  'anthropic-version': '2023-06-01',
58	});
59	
60	// The endpoint a task's hand-off calls, resolved against the repo's config.
61	// Returns `{ name, url, tokenEnv, headers }` or `{ name, error }` — a task naming
62	// an endpoint the repo has not configured is a repo-configuration fact, reported
63	// where the operator reads it, never a crash.
64	export function resolveEndpoint(config, task) {
65	  const name = task?.decl?.invocation_endpoint ?? DEFAULT_ENDPOINT;
66	  // Either spelling: `endpoints` was renamed to say WHICH endpoints these are
67	  // (#1252), and a member writes its own settings, so the old key stays live until
68	  // that member's own converge rewrites it.
69	  const endpoints = config?.taskScheduler?.[ENDPOINTS_KEY] ?? config?.taskScheduler?.[LEGACY_ENDPOINTS_KEY] ?? {};
70	  const entry = endpoints[name];
71	  if (!entry) {
72	    return { name, error: `this repo's settings declare no invocation endpoint "${name}" (taskScheduler.${ENDPOINTS_KEY})` };

# Working in the canary

This repo is Claudinite's **live canary**. Read this before changing anything here, because the
normal instinct — make the repo green, make the repo useful — is wrong in a specific way.

## The gate this repo is half of

Canon CI can prove a canon change is internally consistent. It cannot prove the change is safe for
**consumers**: the vendored mount, the pack loader, the hook wiring and the skill mounts only meet
a real repo on the other side of a vendor set. So the canon runs
`.github/workflows/canary-rehearsal.yml`, which converges *this* repo against a candidate canon ref
and runs the world sweep and the selftest against the result.

The gate's whole value rests on this repo being a **real, disposable member**. Real, or the
rehearsal tests a shape no consumer has. Disposable, or nobody will let the rehearsal converge it.

## What must not be removed

Anything that makes this a member is load-bearing:

- the vendored mount at `.claudinite/shared/` and the `.claudinite-checks.json` declaration
  that names what is vendored;
- the `.claude/settings.json` hook registrations;
- the vendored scheduler workflow, with the repo-hashed cron minute;
- the unfiltered conformance workflow;
- **the `local/canary` pack** — the highest-value shape here. Canon #555 broke the fleet through
  exactly this surface: a local pack's manifest, its rules in both scopes, its bundled skills.

## Reading a red rehearsal

A rehearsal failure is a claim about the **candidate canon ref**, not about this repo. Before
touching anything here, separate the two:

1. **Does the same failure reproduce against canon `main`?** If it does, the canary drifted or
   broke on its own and the candidate ref is exonerated. Re-baseline to `main` and re-run.
2. **Only the candidate ref fails?** That is the signal the gate exists to produce. Fix it in the
   canon. Do not fix it here — a canary patched to stay green is a canary that has stopped
   reporting.
3. **Never quiet a finding with an `accept` entry to get a rehearsal green.** An `accept` is a
   reasoned keep about *this repo's* content; using one to mask a canon regression converts a
   loud failure into a silent one, permanently.

## Repairing the canary

Re-baselining to canon `main` is always the correct repair, and there is no local state here worth
preserving. One caveat, from vendoring's anti-rewind guard (#328): the stamped `ref` in
`.claudinite-checks.json` must be an **ancestor of canon `main`**. Stamp a feature-branch sha and
the repo lands `ref-not-on-trunk`, which convergence then refuses to rewind past — wedging the
repo permanently. Rehearsals may stamp a candidate ref by design; a human repair should not.

# Delivering a scheduled task's pull request

How an executor subagent delivers the PR its task produced — the AGENT lane of the one
delivery procedure. The CODE lane is `land-pr.mjs` beside this file (Action-side workers
run it); **the two must keep saying the same thing** — a nuance changed in one changes in
the other in the same commit. Your GitHub writes go through the session's MCP tools, and
your pushes ride a credential whose events start workflows normally, so — unlike the code
lane — your PR's checks need no help from you to run.

## The task sets the ceiling; the repo decides the rest

Your task's declared `expected_outcome` is a **ceiling, not a plan**:

- **`open-pr`** — open the PR and stop. Never arm auto-merge, never merge. Nothing below
  applies to you.
- **`merged-pr`** — the task *may* land its PR. Whether it actually lands unreviewed is
  **this repo's** setting, read in step 1 — never the task's own knowledge. The same task
  lands itself on one repo and waits for an owner on another, and both are correct.

## 1. Read the repo's delivery preference

`.claudinite-settings.json` → `maintenance.delivery`:

- **`auto-merge`** (legacy aliases `auto`, `push`) — go to step 2.
- **`review`** (legacy alias `pr`) — leave the PR open for the owner and stop. Never arm
  it, never merge it, and never read the standing PR as a failure: degrading `merged-pr`
  to open-pr is the repo's stated intent, and member config wins.
- **Missing or empty** — proceed as `auto-merge` (the default). Do **not** write the key:
  materializing it is the update converge's job, not yours.
- **Anything else** — someone stated an intent you cannot honour, and guessing could
  deliver its opposite. Leave the PR open (the posture that merges nothing) and name the
  unrecognized value in your wrap-up comment on the work item.

## 2. Arm auto-merge

Arm GitHub's native auto-merge on the PR — **squash**, always. Armed → done: GitHub lands
it once this repo's required checks pass.

## 3. When the arm is rejected

Discovered while running item #236 (`claudinite-lifecycle/update`, apply-stage) in a Claude Code cloud/web agent session.

## What happened

`instructions.md` step 6 tells the session to converge its work item by running:

```
node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/converge-item.mjs --issue <n> --outcome ... --summary ... [--pr <n>]
```

`converge-item.mjs`'s `main()` wires this to `makeGh()` from `signals/gh.mjs`, which does a raw `fetch` to `api.github.com` authenticated with `process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN`. In this session type (a Claude Code cloud/web session with the GitHub MCP connector, invoked here via the scheduler's routine-fire endpoint), that call is rejected outright:

```
HTTP 403
{"message":"GitHub access is not enabled for this session. An org admin must connect the Claude GitHub App for this organization.","documentation_url":"https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/github-actions"}
```

This session's only working GitHub channel is the GitHub MCP connector (`mcp__github__*` tools) — consistent with this session's own system instructions ("You do NOT have access to the gh CLI, hub CLI, or direct GitHub API access. Instead, use the GitHub MCP server tools ... for ALL GitHub interactions."). Running `converge-item.mjs` with `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` set fails immediately with `converge-item: #236 could not be read`, because the injected `gh()` never gets a successful response.

## Why this isn't a one-off

The codebase already recognizes this exact split for PR delivery: `land-pr.mjs` is explicitly "Action-side" raw-fetch, and `deliver-pr.md` beside it is the documented **agent-lane MCP twin**, with a comment noting "your GitHub writes go through the session's MCP tools." No equivalent prose or code twin exists for `converge-item.mjs`, even though `instructions.md` (also vendored) directs the session — not an Action — to invoke it directly.

## Impact on this run

Item #236's actual work succeeded (the two withheld workflow files were delivered byte-for-byte, `selftest --strict` and `check_the_world.mjs` passed clean, and PR #237 was merged into `main`). But the session could not perform the terminal convergence in code as instructed, and per the queue instructions ("nothing below is yours to perform... doing it by hand anyway is how an item ends up closed wearing `task:agent`"), it did not hand-rewrite the item's labels/close state either. #236 is being left as-is for the standing executing-leash reclaim to pick up.

## Suggested remedy

Either give `converge-item.mjs` an injectable GitHub client so an agent session can supply one backed by MCP, or add an MCP-lane prose/code twin analogous to `deliver-pr.md`, so `instructions.md` step 6 is actually performable by the session type it's written for.

This is a canon-level (vendored engine) defect — flagging here since this session's GitHub scope is limited to this repo; please relay upstream to Claudinite.
